articles.title: IKEA is Coming to The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim and Fans Are All Saying the Same Thing
articles.summary: IKEA is partnering up with Skyrim in an unexpected collaboration that has fans making the same joke about The Elder Scrolls 6. On September 2, the official IKEA accounts for Ireland and the United Kingdom posted a promotional video on Instagram, showing a mountain of familiar Skyrim memorabilia…
body: For instance, a rune-inscribed Allen wrench is stuffed amongst the frozen Nord helmets, pots, swords, books, and wheels of cheese, while a white Kallax 4x2 shelf sits on top of the pile.

A date is then shown: September 9, 2026, along with the message, “Coming to the Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.” The post’s caption says much the same thing: “A Creation coming to The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.”

Thus far, it’s unclear exactly what this collaboration entails. Does this mean that the Kallax shelf will be available for players to decorate their homes with? Will they be able to use the magic Allen wrench as a weapon? (That would be hilarious.) Or is furniture from the game coming to IKEA?
Either way, fans are all saying the same thing: We’re getting an IKEA collab, of all things, before The Elder Scrolls 6 comes out.

articles.title: Kat Dennings Recalls Her Six-Hour Mad Max: Fury Road Audition With 'Wonderful Person' Tom Hardy
articles.summary: 2 Broke Girls and WandaVision actress Kat Dennings took to social media to recall her experience auditioning opposite Tom Hardy for 2015's Mad Max: Fury Road. Although Dennings at one point likens the audition to being like “an acting class if it was [on] the worst day of your life,” her story…
body: Dennings explained on TikTok how her screen test – she doesn’t specify which role she was up for but presumably it was for one of Immortan Joe’s Brides – took an epic six hours. It was a chemistry read between her and Hardy, who, of course, went on to win the title role of "Mad Max" Rockatansky.

Dennings, who still lived at home with her parents at the time, said director George Miller didn’t do much talking during the audition, with a person she believes was an acting coach leading the process instead.

“The dialogue was a couple of pages, and kind of vague. And basically, what happened was, an acting class, if it was, um, the worst day of your life. At one point, they had us switch roles. They had the camera and had us like running around the corner,” Dennings said.

“The worst part of it, I do believe, was when the acting coach told us to say the lines without saying the lines, encouraging us to just make noises instead of the lines. I was dying. I mean, Tom Hardy, he really took to this exercise. Like, he was able to be extremely free and come up with very creative ways of doing these lines.”

articles.title: CD Projekt Red Is Still Raking In The Cash As We Wait For The Witcher 4
articles.summary: CD Projekt Red has released its latest earnings report for the first half of 2026, and in short, it was a banger of a period for the company, and things are only expected to improve with many big-name releases on the horizon.
body: For the January-July period, CD Projekt Red generated 435 million PLN ($116.4 million USD) in revenue, which was up 23% year-over-year. Additionally, the company posted a net profit of 249 million PLN ($66.6 million USD), which was up 37% year-over-year. Total net profitability for the company was a very impressive 57%.

Management said in its report that these strong results were driven in part by "strong sales" of The Witcher and Cyberpunk games. Additionally, CD Projekt said it benefitted nicely from licensing revenue, a category that is becoming more and more important to the company.

The company specifically called out licensing deals that Cyberpunk 2077 had with games like Wuthering Waves and Apex Legends this year. Additionally, the company pointed out how well Cyberpunk TCG did on Kickstarter.

It would appear that CD Projekt's revenues are only set to grow further in the time ahead. That's because the studio has a lot of big games and content on tap, including The Witcher 3 Remastered this year, The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion in 2027, and then The Witcher 4 in 2028.

articles.title: Sony Is Making 59% More Revenue Per PlayStation User Since PS4 Generation, Says Analyst
articles.summary: Sony is making 59% more money per active PlayStation user now than they were during the PS4 era, according to new data compiled by Niko Partners Director of Research and Insights Daniel Ahmad, who covers the video game market with a focus on the Asia and MENA markets.
body: Responding to a new interview with Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki duscussing why the company isn't as aggressive in marketing the PS5 these days, Ahmad took to X to post, "I did the math on this and average annual revenue per PlayStation active user has grown from 23,580 Yen in FY2018 to 37,485 Yen in FY2025, which is around $230. [It's] an increase of 59% over that period. Although growth was flat over the past year or two."

For more detail and context, he added, "FY19 includes through to March 2020, with Covid leading to a boost in active users. Main drivers here are the transition to higher PS+ tiers, higher spending on game software and DLC / MTX, higher prices for hardware, etc." In short, Ahmad seems to suggest that Sony doesn't need to spend as much money to aggressively market the PS5, in the face of its and every console's rising prices, because it's making more money off of the users it already has.

articles.title: A Playable Build of an Unreleased Scream Game Has Surfaced Thanks to the Steam Leak
articles.summary: An unreleased Scream game has found its way online thanks to the recent Steam leak. Last week, Steam was hit with a massive leak that saw tons of files and builds from the years 2003–2013 dumped online.
body: Kotaku spotted X / Twitter user roly poly reaper talking about the game and sharing never-before-seen gameplay.

Interestingly enough, the game appears to be very similar to the likes of Dead by Daylight. One player would fill the shoes of Ghostface and track down ordinary players who are trying to collect evidence against the killer. The game was in the works from a developer known as Fatshark and would've predated Dead by Daylight and the Friday the 13th games, meaning it was a bit ahead of its time.

It's unclear exactly when this was developed, but it wouldn't be surprising if this took place around the time of Scream 4 in 2011. The franchise had been on ice for a decade prior to that film, so it would make sense if the rights owners were trying to generate some brand synergy. While we'll never get to play the finished version of this Scream game, some of the fans digging through the files were able to get multiplayer working.

The sign-up sheet, which is now closed, asks a few different questions of potential testers. The most important is if they are willing to sign an NDA, so don't expect news to come out of the closed beta.

articles.title: A Real-Life Romance (And The Love Of Fans) Fueled A Classic NES Remake
articles.summary: With headlines dominated by stories of buyouts, layoffs, employee mistreatment, and crunch, it's easy to think that game development is a constant parade of misery and strife.
body: The Battle of Olympus is a side-scrolling action-RPG released in 1988 by Broderbund for the NES. The visuals and gameplay take a lot of cues from Zelda II, though with a Greek mythology-inspired story and setting and a pretty solid challenge level throughout. It's been described as "a hidden gem" of the NES library many times, often overshadowed by similar titles, but beloved by those who enjoyed it.

Notably, The Battle of Olympus was developed in Japan by a very small developer named Infinity. How small? Well, the game's credits list a whopping three different people--Yukio Horimoto, Reiko Oshida, and Kazuo Sawa. Yukio and Reiko were the two main collaborators, with Yukio handling programming, Reiko on art design, and the pair working together on the game's story. As it turns out, the project would lead the two to discover their connection to each other, and they would marry soon after--making it very fitting that The Battle of Olympus's Japanese subtitle is "The Legend of Love."

articles.title: Resident Evil Director Says There’s “No Chance” He’d Survive His Own Movie
articles.summary: Resident Evil games over the years have slowly added more fantastical elements to their tale of bioweapons running amok, but for the new live-action movie, director Zach Cregger is dialing back those ideas to a more "grounded" level.
body: "I feel like some of the Resident Evil games get a little magical," Cregger said during a Reddit Ask Me Anything session (via YouTuber Troy Hill Talks Movies ).

"[Resident Evil] 8, we have a woman who can turn into a bird and fly around. And like, I love it. I've played it a bunch of times. I think it's an awesome game, but in terms of me making a movie out of it, it's like I've got to try and limit some of the wild aspects of Resident Evil. And so I chose to stick with the T-Virus, keep it as grounded as possible. So that means I'm not going to have a gigantic jacked dude in a trench coat, because I'm like, where'd the coat come from? How did he get the coat?"

Cregger explained that while the Resident Evil games do explain how Mr. X gets his stylish coat, in the world he has constructed for the movie, there's no time for the infected bioweapons to consider zombie apocalypse fashion. "This movie, it's like the outbreak just happened," Cregger added. "I want to keep it chaotic, I want to keep it primal, and I want to just keep it as grounded as I can. The T-Virus causes all kinds of cool, fun mutations. That is enough, so I'm limiting it there."

articles.title: Kingdom Hearts almost led to Disney making its own version of Super Smash Bros, former dev says
articles.summary: Kingdom Hearts bashing together a bunch of Disney's best toys (and being quite successful in the process) led the Mouse House to briefly begin work on a crossover fighting game in the style of Super Smash Bros.
body: That's according to Ken Christiansen, a former Disney Interactive concept artist who also had credits on the very first Kingdom Hearts game. In an interview with Time Extension, the developer said Kingdom Hearts' world-hopping shenanigans opened Disney's eyes to a whole universe of potential crossover projects.

The development of the original Kingdom Hearts game was apparently a little difficult "because Disney was so reluctant to have that possibility of crossing over The Lion King into The Little Mermaid world," Christiansen recalled.

Disney supposedly "couldn't get over" seeing its most popular characters run into each other constantly, and the company's hesitance meant there was "just a little bit of butting heads" during production, even if most of the developers "thought it was the greatest idea in the world."

Regardless of how unexcited certain Disney executives were about Square Enix 's still-whacky series, it was a pretty major success. The first Kingdom Hearts became one of the PlayStation 2's best-selling games and, as you can imagine, put dollar signs in the eyes of company higher ups.

articles.title: 10 The Blood of Dawnwalker beginner's tips to help you defeat Brencis
articles.summary: These beginner's tips for The Blood of Dawnwalker will improve your dawn-walking adventure in the vampire-ridden Vale Sangora. Don't let Coen's dual nature or the 30-day calendar intimidate you; once you understand the mechanics, questing, exploring, and gearing up will be a breeze.
body: Here are our best tips on how to handle the time mechanic, prepare for the final confrontation, unlock the best abilities, and boost the fun in The Blood of Dawnwalker.

In The Blood of Dawnwalker, time moves forward when you take certain actions, such as speaking with NPCs, battling enemies, and upgrading abilities. This means that spending time on one activity may not leave time for another, which is especially true during the game's prologue. Luckily, the game always warns you of the time cost beforehand (see your journal or the time bar in the top right of the screen), so you're free to explore an area, chat with several people, and obtain several quests before committing to a time-consuming activity.

Since time is scarce during the prologue, consider running around Laslea Glen, talking to everyone, before pursuing any of the quests you've obtained. You won't be as hard-pressed for time in the open world, but it's still a good idea to get a sense of available activities before committing to one.

articles.title: Iconic Banjo-Kazooie composer is more hopeful about a sequel these days, but knows "like three companies" have already been turned down
articles.summary: Grant Kirkhope - the iconic video game composer behind the Donkey Kong Rap and the Banjo-Kazooie games - thinks a potential Banjo-Threeie is slightly more likely now.
body: Almost three decades have passed since Banjo-Kazooie's last mainline platformer flapped onto the N64 and it's been almost 20 years since Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts flopped onto the Xbox 360, but it's never too late for another adventure with the bird and bear.

Speaking to FRVR, Kirkhope explained that he used to feel there was "zero chance of another Banjo-Kazooie game." Nowadays, that sentiment's been upgraded to a "slight chance" because he thinks Rare's updated leadership could be more receptive to an outside developer spearheading a threequel.

"Rare just typically say no to everything," the composer explained. "I've known people present cartoons to them, all sorts of ideas, and they just say no to everything." But since former studio head Craig Duncan stepped down from his role at Xbox Game Studios, Kirkhope reckons Rare might be "a little bit different right now" and "a bit more open to discussion."

articles.title: How to beat the Ravenous Bear and complete Into the Den in The Blood of Dawnwalker
articles.summary: Fighting the Ravenous Bear is an early combat challenge in Blood of Dawnwalker 's prologue, but mainly because you don't have many skills or decent equipment yet, which turns the fight into a slog. After you do defeat it, you'll also have to track down a treasure as part of the Into the Den quest.
body: With all that, you should be able to defeat the bear, and then check the mangled corpse behind it to start the Into the Den quest.

Reading the Tattered Letter you find on the corpse will begin Into the Den, giving you a search area to the northwest where you need to look for the stash mentioned in the note. Specifically, you're looking for a "flat stone marked with an X".

You can find this inside in the ramshackle hut with the door on the west side of the search area —it's the only structure with a door, so it's hard to miss. If still confused, follow the nearby shrine west along the road and you'll spot the hut to your left as you pass.

Loot the treasure (which will take one time cycle) to get the very snazzy-looking Artisan's Tunic, the extremely good Rebel's Falchion shortsword, plus a handy note about where to sell any silver you might find later in the game, a substance strictly prohibited by the vamps for obvious reasons.

videos.title: Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance - Boosted Action Overview | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Ascend to Master Rank with the Boost Bracer, a new hunting action that expands the abilities of each of the 14 weapon types in Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance.
body: Build Boost Bracer energy by staying aggressive with your attacks, then activate Boost with a special Boost Driver attack, or other unique actions per weapon. Boost enables abilities such as new combos and enhanced attacks, allowing you to seize control of the powerful threats that await you.
*Footage represents a game still in development. The main Monster Hunter Wilds game is required to play Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance.

videos.title: Ontos - Extended Gameplay Reveal | PS5 Games
videos.summary: An extended look into Crombie’s experiment.
body: In ONTOS, you play as Aditi as she explores the repurposed moon hotel Samsara and encounters strange Experiments and other disturbing scenarios. Your morality will be tested.
In this video, we’ll take you deeper into one such experiment led by Crombie, a scientist drawn to Samsara in search of answers about the essence of one’s unique, individual self.
Do you trust the machine? Do you seek an alternative approach?
